overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of how AI progress is measured and how AI systems are used in AI research. You'll be asked about what a benchmark measures, contamination and saturation, time-horizon and productivity measures, and the difference between bounded self-refinement and open-ended self-improvement.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A news story says a new AI model scored 92 percent on a bar exam. What does the score show?

options.html: That the model could now practice law without supervision
options.text: That the model could now practice law without supervision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A benchmark score describes performance on its own tasks under its own conditions. The model answered exam questions well, and the exam doesn't test the rest of a lawyer's work.

options.html: That the model answered that exam's questions well
options.text: That the model answered that exam's questions well
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A score describes performance on those tasks under those conditions. How far it carries over to real work is a separate question about the test's validity.

options.html: That the model understands law in the way a lawyer does
options.text: That the model understands law in the way a lawyer does
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. An exam score doesn't settle that. It shows that the model answered that exam's questions well, under the conditions of the test.

options.html: That the model will outperform lawyers within a few years
options.text: That the model will outperform lawyers within a few years
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That would be a forecast, and a single score can't support it. The score shows that the model answered that exam's questions well.

forms.stemHtml: A benchmark's questions have been posted online for years. A new model scores far higher on it than on a freshly written test of the same skill. What most likely explains the gap?

options.html: Saturation, since top models all score near the maximum
options.text: Saturation, since top models all score near the maximum
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Saturation describes scores bunching at the ceiling. A high score on public questions with a lower score on fresh ones points to contamination: the public questions were probably in the training data.

options.html: Selection bias, since the test-takers weren't representative
options.text: Selection bias, since the test-takers weren't representative
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Selection bias concerns who or what is included in a study. A high score on public questions with a lower score on fresh ones points to contamination: the public questions were probably in the training data.

options.html: Contamination, since the questions were in training data
options.text: Contamination, since the questions were in training data
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! When test items appear in training data, a model can reproduce answers without being able to solve new problems of the same kind.

options.html: External validity, since the model was tested in a laboratory
options.text: External validity, since the model was tested in a laboratory
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. External validity is about whether a result holds outside a study's conditions. A high score on public questions with a lower score on fresh ones points to contamination.

forms.stemHtml: A report says an AI model has a time horizon of two hours on software tasks. What does that mean?

options.html: The model takes about two hours to finish a software task
options.text: The model takes about two hours to finish a software task
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The time is the human's. A two-hour time horizon means the model succeeds about half the time on tasks that take a skilled person two hours.

options.html: The model can work reliably for two hours without supervision
options.text: The model can work reliably for two hours without supervision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The bar is 50 percent success, which is far from reliable. It means the model succeeds about half the time on tasks that take a skilled person two hours.

options.html: The model does two hours of any worker's job as well as that worker would
options.text: The model does two hours of any worker's job as well as that worker would
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The measure covers defined software tasks and a 50 percent bar. It means the model succeeds about half the time on tasks that take a skilled person two hours.

options.html: The model succeeds half the time on tasks that take people two hours
options.text: The model succeeds half the time on tasks that take people two hours
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A time horizon is measured in the time a skilled person needs, at a 50 percent success bar, on a particular set of tasks.

forms.stemHtml: A research agent rewrites its own program code over several days and keeps each change that scores better on a hidden set of tests. Which statements about this are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It is an example of bounded self-refinement
options.text: It is an example of bounded self-refinement
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The system improves its surrounding code against a fixed outside check, which is the bounded kind.

options.html: People chose the tasks and built the tests it was judged by
options.text: People chose the tasks and built the tests it was judged by
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The evaluator came from outside the loop, and that is what keeps the improvement measurable.

options.html: It shows that open-ended self-improvement has been achieved
options.text: It shows that open-ended self-improvement has been achieved
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No published work shows a system setting its own research direction and improving without limit. This demonstration has an evaluator and bounds that people set.

options.html: It proves that AI progress will now speed up without limit
options.text: It proves that AI progress will now speed up without limit
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That is a forecast, and researchers disagree about it. The demonstration shows a bounded loop working within limits that people set.

forms.stemHtml: In a 2025 trial, experienced developers took 19 percent longer on tasks when AI tools were allowed. What is the soundest conclusion?

options.html: Benefit in use can differ from capability on a test
options.text: Benefit in use can differ from capability on a test
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A system can complete defined test tasks and still fail to speed people up in a given setting. The two are separate measurements.

options.html: AI tools make every software developer slower at every task
options.text: AI tools make every software developer slower at every task
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The trial had 16 developers on projects they knew very well, and its authors warn against generalizing. It shows that benefit in use can differ from capability on a test.

options.html: Time-horizon measurements must have been wrong
options.text: Time-horizon measurements must have been wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The two studies measure different things. The trial shows that benefit in use can differ from capability on a test.

options.html: Developers can judge accurately how much AI helps
options.text: Developers can judge accurately how much AI helps
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The developers believed AI had sped them up when it had slowed them down. The trial shows that benefit in use can differ from capability on a test.

title: Measuring progress and AI-assisted AI research
